headline: A shared-inference cost study finds allocation rules shift tenant bills by 12–14 points
summary: The paper introduces unalloc, which joins Kubernetes OpenCost allocations, LiteLLM gateway logs and OpenAI/Anthropic provider cost data to expose unattributed spend and reconcile it against invoices. Its accounting examples include synthetic billing fixtures: in one constructed deployment, owner labels only on leader pods left 66% of GPU spend unowned, while a fallback assigned 61% to a Helm chart label. Separately, a paper-reported H100/vLLM test found that token-based allocation assigned a retrieval-heavy tenant 12–14 percentage points more of a shared bill than equal time-share allocation across tested loads. The authors say neither meter is a ground truth; the repository describes one model and one two-minute run per load. These results show that labels, source overlap and allocation rules can change reported cost ownership, not that they change total compute expense or establish a uniquely correct cost split.
